# Story 56.01 — A play queue on the server

> Epic 56 · Phase 1 · Depends on: — · Needed by: 56.02, 56.10, 56.11, 56.12, 56.13, Epic 55

## Why

Play all and Shuffle need a queue that can hold a whole library, survive the app closing and
move between devices. Today the only queue is the web's, in one tab's `sessionStorage`, and
Shuffle is one random page of `GET /api/videos` (`sort=random` has no cursor), so a TV cannot
shuffle a library of thousands of videos. Plex keeps play queues on the server; so will Maktaba.

# Story 56.02 — Play and Shuffle on the TVs

> Epic 56 · Phase 3 · Depends on: 56.01, 56.03 · Needed by: 56.11

## Why

A library, a series, a season, a collection and a playlist on a TV can only be played one video
at a time. Plex puts Play and Shuffle on each of them; people expect to start a library on
shuffle from the couch and leave it.

# Story 56.07 — Plex collections, read into Maktaba

> Epic 56 · Phase 2 · Depends on: 56.06 (slot 0186) · Needed by: 56.08

## Why

A home that used Plex before Maktaba has collections there that people made by hand over
years. Maktaba already indexes Plex (`plex_index` fills `plex_items`, rating key ↔ video) and
writes its own season and topic collections into Plex (`plex_collection`, `plex_groups`), but
never reads Plex's collections back. Moving from Plex should not lose them.

# Story 56.09 — Smart playlists

> Epic 56 · Phase 1 · Depends on: — (slot 0185) · Needed by: 56.10, 56.12, 56.13

## Why

Playlists today are manual lists (`user_playlists`, slot 0162). Plex also has smart playlists: a
saved filter with a sort and a limit, that keeps itself up to date, per user. Viewers cannot make
collections (admin-only, README §11 decision 3), so smart playlists are how a viewer keeps
"unwatched lessons of speaker X, newest first" one click away, on every device.
